name: NATS
description: NATS server reads over its monitoring HTTP endpoint: server identity and load, current client connections, subscription counts, JetStream usage and known routes. Read-only; the monitoring endpoint exposes no write surface, and this connector wires none. It is unauthenticated by default (base_url is the only credential); put it behind a reverse proxy for exposure beyond a trusted LAN.

tools.name: server_info
tools.description: Get the NATS server's identity, version, resource usage and message/connection totals

tools.name: connections
tools.description: List the client connections currently open on this server

tools.name: subscriptions
tools.description: Get subscription counts and interest-cache stats for this server

tools.name: jetstream
tools.description: Get JetStream usage: memory and storage totals, accounts, streams, consumers and message/byte counts

tools.name: routes
tools.description: List the cluster routes this server knows about

needs_review: AUTH IS none BY DESIGN: NATS's monitoring HTTP port (default 8222) ships with no authentication of its own, so base_url is the only credential and auth.type is 'none'. Client-protocol auth (the NATS wire protocol on 4222) is a separate, unmodelled surface.
READ-ONLY: all five tools are GET, write:false. The monitoring endpoint has no mutating surface to model.
jetstream returns a 200 with near-empty counters when JetStream is enabled but unused, and a minimal envelope if JetStream is disabled entirely; both are valid live proofs, not failures.
routes returns an empty routes array on a standalone (non-clustered) server; that is a valid 200 proof of the endpoint, not a routing gap.
LIVE-PROOF CONTRACT: every tool takes no input, so every _probe is {}. Proven against docker nats:2.10, then destroyed.
